title: Invertibility of integral sections on a closed geometric fibre
statement: Let A be a strictly henselian local ring and Λ a commutative ring. Let p:Z→Spec A be integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], Ω algebraically closed, and t:Spec Ω→Spec A send its unique point to the closed point. For any Cartesian square (i:Z′→Z,p′:Z′→Spec Ω,p,t) [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and every sheaf F of Λ-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical global-section restriction globalSectionsUpperStarMap along i is an isomorphism. No strict-henselization construction, stalk comparison, or neighbourhood formula occurs in this statement.

proof.text: Integrality over affine Spec A makes Z affine Spec B, with B integral over A. Set J=m_A B. The pair (A,m_A) is henselian, and the integral-over-henselian-pair theorem gives HenselianRing B J.
Apply the degree-zero henselian comparison to the proper identity of Spec B and the ideal J. Restriction to Spec(B/J) is an isomorphism.

The closed-image condition gives kernel m_A for A→Ω, hence a factorization through the separably closed residue field k=A/m_A. Pullback pasting identifies Z′ with the base change of Spec(B/J) to Ω. The field-extension section theorem gives a set bijection; the module/set comparison, including its unit equation, transports this to the module restriction.

Composition of inverse-image units and the global-section composition formula identify the composite of these two restrictions with the displayed map, up to the canonical isomorphisms. A bijective module homomorphism is invertible. The same argument includes B=0 and Λ=0.
